issues: Assumed 'free' means no person is seated or standing at the table; dishes, bags or reserved signs left on an empty table are not treated as occupied.
Occupancy is judged per frame from person-table overlap, so a waiter or guest walking past may briefly mark a table as occupied. A short debounce reduces this.
Assumed a fixed camera covering the dining area, with tables visible from an elevated angle.
summary: Detect restaurant tables in a fixed camera view and classify each as free (no one at it) or occupied (people seated at it).

classes.name: table_free
classes.description: A restaurant table with no person seated or standing at it.

classes.name: table_occupied
classes.description: A restaurant table with at least one person seated or standing directly at it.

event_rules.description: Report a table as free once it has had no person at it for several consecutive frames, so passers-by do not cause flicker.

visual_conditions: Daytime natural light and evening artificial or dim ambient lighting
Tables of different sizes and shapes (round, square, long, booth)
Partially occluded tables behind seated guests, staff or chairs
Tables at near and far distances from the camera
Empty tables with leftover dishes, glasses or bags
Staff walking past or standing beside tables
Busy periods with crowded dining room and quiet periods with mostly empty tables
Single guests and large groups at a table
test_scenarios: Recording of a full lunch service on a different day from training footage
Evening dinner service with dim, warm lighting
Footage from a second camera angle or a different section of the dining room
Clean-up period with empty tables that still have dishes on them
Busy period with waiters frequently walking between tables
synthetic_targets: Dim evening or candle-lit lighting variants
Strong window glare and backlit daytime scenes
Empty tables with leftover plates, cups and napkins
Different table cloths, colours and furniture styles
Crowded scenes with heavy occlusion of tables by people
